label: Task 1 route (straight A to B with checkpoints): read by Python (task_route.py, bridge.server --task Task1) and by the Unity side (TrialRunner, Task1Route, and the scene builder that places the Task 1 workers). Per-task config of Task 1; its sha256 is in configs/hri_frozen.json -> tasks.Task1.
declared: 2026-10-21, before any Task 1 final run (declared design change, AUDIT.md section 9). Task 2 does not read this file.
rule: The straight line of the roadmap: from the start node, its only branch, then the FORWARD branch of each junction, until an endpoint (A -> J1 -> E1). That line is cut into checkpoints + 1 equal parts; the cut points are the checkpoints, named C1..Cn from the start. A checkpoint within merge_with_junction_m of a junction on the line is that junction (it keeps its name and its other branches). Every junction on the line is a stop as well. Default 3: C1 (6.25, -5), J1 (6.25, 0), C3 (6.25, 5).
workers_rule: A worker stands at every stop (the same Mixamo avatar as in Task 2, one instance per stop, built into the scene by Tools > Warehouse HRI > Add Worker and Roadmap, active only in Task 1 sessions), worker_ahead_m ahead of the stop and worker_right_m to the right of the arrival direction, facing the arriving robot, and shows FORWARD for the whole trial. Default positions: C1 (8.75, -4), J1 (8.75, 1), C3 (8.75, 6). Changed 2026-10-21 (declared design change, before any Task 1 final): before, one worker was moved from stop to stop by the roadmap rule (2.5 m ahead and right).
workers_why: One standing worker per checkpoint, as requested by the owner. Not the roadmap's 2.5 m ahead / 2.5 m right: with 5 m between stops the worker just passed would be exactly as far from the next stop as that stop's worker (3.54 m both), and the frozen scan picks the nearest person. With 1.0 m ahead / 2.5 m right the stop's own worker is at 2.69 m and the previous one at 4.72 m (the next one at 6.50 m). 2.5 m to the side keeps every worker clear of the robot's straight path (at least 1.9 m from its centre line after the read, against the frozen 0.6 m path corridor), so the robot passes the worker it has just asked.
why: More worker interactions per Task 1 trial (3 instead of 1) for the gesture-reading baseline, on the same straight A to B route and the same B. The checkpoints are stops on the robot's map, like junctions; they carry no information about B (every checkpoint has only a FORWARD branch, and J1 keeps its LEFT and RIGHT branches).
